A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same ToolHop benchmark. Their main text, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching material across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original evaluations of 14 LLMs in Table 4, feedback experiments in Table 5, and dataset analyses and case studies.

after.justification: V3 retains those empirical results and adds evaluations with alternative inference frameworks and two additional models in Appendix E.

M1.justification: The query-driven tool creation, document refinement, and code generation pipeline is unchanged, including its construction prompts and example code. ReAct and CodeAct are added evaluation frameworks.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 995 MoreHopQA-derived queries and 3,912 tools across 47 domains. The added experiments retain ToolHop; Appendix A's statement about ongoing expansion does not document additional evaluated coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix E/Table 11 adds ReAct and CodeAct comparisons across the original 14 models, plus ToolLLaMA-2 7B-v2 and TL-CodeLLaMA-2 7B. This substantially broadens the evaluated comparison methods beyond the original native function-calling evaluations.

E3.justification: V3 adds systematic evaluation using ReAct and CodeAct inference procedures alongside native function-calling templates. The original direct, mandatory, and free scenarios, metrics, and documented decoding settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E newly examines sensitivity to inference framework across all original model families, testing how strongly performance depends on the interaction procedure. The existing feedback ablation in Table 5 and case studies in Figures 7–10 are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, or statistical significance tests. The added results retain point-estimate reporting; Table 4's averages are across models.

E6.justification: Tables 4 and 5 are numerically identical. New Table 11 adds ReAct and CodeAct results and two specialized-model scores; for example, ReAct accuracy is 57.79 for LLaMA3.1-Instruct-70B and 54.17 for GPT-4o. Its FC column repeats the existing Free-scenario scores, so the additions are results under different procedures.

T1.justification: The task, tool, and parameter definitions in Section 2.1 and the construction formulation in Section 2.2 are unchanged. No theoretical assumptions, proofs, or derivations are added.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the benchmark's scope, three-stage construction contribution, and claims about multi-hop difficulty and model-family differences. The headline evaluation of 14 models and GPT-4o's 49.04% result also remain unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix E adds explanations connecting ReAct's explicit reasoning to open-source model planning and framework preferences to training differences. Appendix A adds benchmark-longevity arguments. The original family-level interpretations and Limitations section are otherwise retained.

D1.justification: The abstract's displayed access URL and embedded hyperlink change to the Hugging Face dataset-specific route. Existing construction prompts, code examples, model descriptions, and decoding disclosures are retained; the added framework experiments provide little implementation detail.

R1.justification: New Appendix A/Table 6 systematically positions ToolHop against 12 benchmarks, explicitly distinguishing its feature combination from BFCL v3 and other alternatives. Additional benchmark and framework references substantially expand this positioning; the ToolEyes publication update represents the same cited work.

P1.justification: Section 3.1 is condensed and its model descriptions move to Appendix D. V3 adds appendix sections and acknowledgments, updates author information, and makes limited prose edits while preserving most language and the main narrative structure.

P2.justification: V3 adds the benchmark comparison matrix in Table 6 and framework results in Table 11. Existing figures and main result-table designs are retained, with prompt-table renumbering and localized changes to page flow.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the evaluation more informative by testing dependence on inference framework and providing explicit benchmark comparisons. These useful additions have limits: framework implementation details remain sparse, and Appendix E overgeneralizes the GPT preference for ReAct—GPT-3.5-Turbo scores 36.58 with FC versus 28.14 with ReAct. The evidence supports a limited net quality gain.
